summary: Original ground lookout on Highland (Red) Mtn near Butte; sources date it to 1933 or 1939, a 1953 lightning strike hit it, and the site is listed as gone.

facts.status_note: The register listing marks this original ground site as gone. No source dates its removal.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest

events.note: Register says an L-4 groundhouse was built in 1933; a lookout history page dates the development to about 1933.
Montana Standard reports from September and October 1939 describe CCC crews completing a new lookout station on Highland peak. This conflicts with the 1933 date.
Don McPherson served as a lookout atop Red Mountain that summer.
A lightning bolt hit the lookout that summer, broke more than 70 panes of glass and caused an estimated $1,500 in damage.
The 1954 L-4 cab on a concrete base replaced the 1933 groundhouse, about a quarter mile north of the Red Mountain summit.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and lookout history page date the first L-4 structure to 1933; 1939 Montana Standard reports describe a new station completed by CCC crews. Not resolved by the sources. The story reports both.
Register and lookout page say 15 miles south of Butte; a 1939 Montana Standard report says 20 miles. The story gives the register figure and notes the other.
Register calls the 1933 building a ground-level L-4 groundhouse; a 1956 survey description of the Red Mountain tower says a small white cabin on pole legs. Not resolved. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Loc 1 is the original ground site listed as gone. The standing 1954 cab (NHLR US 927) is a separate record and is covered only as the replacement. No source dates the removal of the original or describes what remains there. The 1933 vs 1939 start date is unresolved, and I could not confirm whether the 1939 station is the same building. The brief's Loc 1 coordinates match the Montana list. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook post (search snippet only, not read) mentions Forest Service talks about a future project at Highland (Red); it is not used. Access to the 1954 cab is unclear beyond 'available for emergencies'.
